title: Async Pipeline Generator
problemStatement: Implement an async generator `asyncTransformStream(items, transformFn)` that consumes an array of items, applies async `transformFn(item)` to each sequentially, and yields each result.
interviewTrap: Using `items.forEach(async ...)` inside an async generator does not pause generator iteration properly.

testCases.name: Transforms and yields items sequentially
testCases.testFn: const res = []; for await (const val of asyncTransformStream([1, 2, 3], async x => x * 2)) { res.push(val); } return res;

testCases.name: Handles empty array stream
testCases.testFn: const res = []; for await (const val of asyncTransformStream([], async x => x)) { res.push(val); } return res;

testCases.name: Handles async delays between yields
testCases.testFn: const res = []; const delay = ms => new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, ms)); for await (const v of asyncTransformStream(['a', 'b'], async s => { await delay(5); return s.toUpperCase(); })) { res.push(v); } return res;

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: An Async Pipeline Generator combines async generators (`async function*`) with streaming data transformations. It yields items asynchronously, consuming upstream asynchronous data feeds with backpressure.
stepByStepWalkthrough: Iterate over input stream using `for await (const item of asyncIterable)`.
Pipe the item sequentially through each transformation function: `let val = item; for (const fn of transformFns) val = await fn(val)`.
Consumers pull transformed values one-by-one, pausing the upstream pipeline until requested.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: Async generators implement the AsyncIterator protocol (`[Symbol.asyncIterator]`), returning promises for each `{ value, done }` iteration step. This natively supports backpressure: if a downstream consumer is slow, the upstream generator waits at `yield` before pulling more data.

complexity.time: O(N * M) where N is item count and M is number of transform stages.

edgeCasesHandled: Empty stream produces zero yields and terminates with `{ done: true }`.
Asynchronous delays inside transform functions are properly awaited.
Errors in transforms reject downstream consumers safely.

specifications: ECMA-262 §27.6 AsyncGeneratorFunction Objects and AsyncIterator Protocol
verifiedRules: Async iterators return a Promise resolving to an IteratorResult.
Execution only advances when downstream invokes .next(), providing natural backpressure.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What is Backpressure and how do Async Generators handle it natively?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: Backpressure occurs when a data producer produces data faster than a downstream consumer can process it. Async generators (`async function*`) solve this natively through 'pull-based' iteration: the upstream generator pauses at `yield` and NEVER produces the next chunk until the consumer calls `await iterator.next()`, preventing memory buffer bloat.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: High-level systems question on stream flow control.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What does [Symbol.asyncIterator] return compared to [Symbol.iterator]?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: `[Symbol.iterator]` returns an iterator whose `.next()` returns `{ value, done }`. `[Symbol.asyncIterator]` returns an async iterator whose `.next()` returns a `Promise<{ value, done }>`, consumed via `for await (const x of stream)`.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Verifies standard async iterator protocol knowledge.

realWorldUseCases.scenario: Streaming Large CSV / JSON Lines Files
realWorldUseCases.description: Node.js pipelines parse 10GB log files line-by-line using async generators without loading the file into memory.
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: for await (const line of readLines(file)) { process(line); }

realWorldUseCases.description: Modern chat applications use async generators to yield LLM response tokens to the UI as they arrive over HTTP SSE streams.
realWorldUseCases.companies: OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Vercel AI SDK
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: for await (const chunk of streamText()) { appendToUI(chunk); }

howToExplain.opening: Async Pipeline Generators combine async/await with generators to create pull-based streaming pipelines with built-in backpressure.
keyPoints: Async iterables implement [Symbol.asyncIterator] and return promises for each iteration step.
Naturally throttles producers to match consumer processing speed (backpressure).
Consumed seamlessly with for await...of loops.
Ideal for streaming large datasets, file I/O, and LLM token responses.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Pull-based async iteration eliminates out-of-memory crashes when processing data streams that exceed physical RAM.
analogies: Drinking through a straw: you pull a sip when you're ready to swallow; the cup doesn't dump all the liquid down your throat at once.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using standard Array.prototype.forEach with async callbacks.
commonMistakes.why: forEach does not await async callbacks; it fires all iterations concurrently and ignores returned promises.
commonMistakes.correct: Use for await...of or sequential while loops with async generators.

followUpDeepDive.question: How does the WHATWG ReadableStream integrate with Async Iterators?
followUpDeepDive.answer: Modern browsers and Node 18+ implement `ReadableStream.prototype[Symbol.asyncIterator]`, allowing any fetch response body stream (`response.body`) to be directly consumed via `for await (const chunk of response.body)`.
